candidate.title: SINC-seq
candidate.scope: The assigned central SINC-seq row: single-cell integrated nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA sequencing, with microfluidic separation of a retained nucleus and ITP-extracted cytRNA followed by separate SMART-Seq2-labeled cDNA library branches. The left two-RNA drawing is an analyte overview. The two final libraries support matched compartment-expression comparisons. SMART-Seq2 is an embedded component, not another target method. Neighboring RamDA-seq and viscRNA-seq rows and the right-hand chemical catalogue are outside this card. Primary-paper details clarify the depicted implementation and sequencing-ready endpoint; no unshown adaptations or complete laboratory recipe are asserted.

states.label: Single cell containing nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA
features: The left-hand explanatory overview depicts nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA separately, each with an AA(A)n tail; this depiction does not establish comprehensive measurement of nonpolyadenylated RNA.
These two RNA drawings describe the biological targets; they are not additional alternative assay workflows.
The actual preparation starts from one cell, preserving the pairing of its two eventual fractions.

operations.label: Lysis and ITP extraction
operations.description: Selectively lyses the cell membrane and initiates ITP extraction of released cytRNA. Produces a retained RNA-containing nucleus and a spatially separate focused cytRNA zone.
operations.mechanism: An electric field concentrated at the hydrodynamic trap lyses the cytoplasmic membrane while leaving the nuclear membrane relatively intact. ITP collects and focuses released cytRNA at the electrolyte interface.
operations.information_effect: Introduces compartment-specific physical separation while preserving the same-cell relationship between the two output branches; the intended separation is not a claim of perfect recovery or zero contamination.

operations.label: nucRNA-Seq by SMART-Seq2
operations.description: Uses the separately recovered nuclear fraction as the RNA source for an off-chip cDNA library workflow, changing the nuclear RNA readout substrate into the upper sequencing-ready cDNA-derived DNA library. The diagram groups library construction in this single block.
operations.mechanism: The paper reports separate cDNA synthesis using the named Smart-seq2 component, cDNA amplification, and Nextera XT tagmentation for sequencing libraries. These clarify the broad endpoint without adding unshown internal operation nodes.
operations.information_effect: cDNA sequence represents captured nuclear transcripts and supports gene-expression and intron-retention readouts at the coverage supported by this implementation. Keeping this library paired with its cytRNA library enables the captioned nucleus/cytoplasm expression comparison.

method_scopes.rationale: The card title and matching row explicitly identify SINC-seq, expanded in the figure as single-cell integrated nucRNA and cytRNA sequencing. All six local operations apply to this depicted SINC-seq implementation, including both independent library branches. The two branch-recovery instances describe coupled physical separation without asserting pooling. Abdelmoez et al. confirms the same retained-nucleus/ITP-cytRNA architecture and separate off-chip libraries; this establishes the paper association for SINC-seq. It does not make SMART-Seq2 or neighboring catalogue assays additional targets.
